subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: with an adult, you set a camera on a steady stand at a window or in the courtyard, pointing at the northern sky, and take a photo that stays open for several hours. What pattern will the stars make, and which star stays almost still?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: kisi bade ke saath, camera ko khidki ya aangan mein ek stand pe uttar ke aasmaan ki taraf rakh ke kai ghanton ki ek photo li. Taare kaisa pattern banayenge, aur kaunsa taara lagbhag wahin rahega?
answer: The stars draw circular trails (arcs) around one point; the Pole Star stays almost at the centre.

subject: science
prompt_en: You found the Pole Star using the pointer stars. Why does the Pole Star help travellers find north?
prompt_hi: Tumne pointer taaron se Dhruva tara dhundha. Dhruva tara yatriyon ko north dhundhne mein kyon madad karta hai?
answer: It lies almost straight above the Earth's North Pole, nearly in line with the Earth's axis, so it stays nearly fixed in the northern sky while other stars move.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare the Sun with a star you see at night. How are they alike, and why do they look so different?
prompt_hi: Suraj aur raat mein dikhne wale kisi taare ko compare karo. Dono ek jaise kaise hain, aur itne alag kyon dikhte hain?
answer: Both are stars, hot glowing balls of gas. The Sun is much nearer, so it looks big and bright; the other stars are much farther away and look like dots.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why can't we see stars on a clear, sunny afternoon, but can see them at night from the same place?
prompt_hi: Saaf dhoop wali dopahar mein taare kyon nahi dikhte, jabki usi jagah se raat mein dikh jaate hain?
answer: The stars are there all day, but sunlight scattered by the air makes the sky so bright that their faint light is hidden; at night the sky is dark.

subject: science
prompt_en: Long ago, sailors and camel caravans crossing the Thar desert at night used the stars. How could they keep heading north?
prompt_hi: Bahut pehle naavik aur Thar registaan paar karte oont ke kaafile raat mein taaron ka sahara lete the. Woh north ki taraf kaise chalte rehte the?
answer: They found the Pole Star (using Saptarishi's pointer stars) and travelled towards it, because it stays fixed in the north.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw the seven stars of Saptarishi as dots joined by lines. Mark the two pointer stars and draw an arrow from them to the Pole Star.
prompt_hi: Saptarishi ke saat taaron ko bindu bana ke lakeeron se jodo. Do pointer taare mark karo aur unse Dhruva tare tak teer banao.
answer: A ladle (or question-mark) shape; the two pointer stars are at the outer edge of the bowl, far from the handle; the arrow runs from them to the Pole Star, about five times the gap between them.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'I saw a star fall from the sky last night! Shooting stars are stars dropping down.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Kal raat maine ek taara aasmaan se girte dekha! Toote taare asli taare hote hain jo neeche girte hain.' Galti kya hai?
answer: A shooting star is a meteor: a small piece of rock or dust from space burning up in Earth's air. Real stars are huge and very far away and don't fall.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your younger sister why stars seem to move across the night sky, and why one star, Dhruva tara, seems to stay in place.
prompt_hi: Apni chhoti behen ko samjhao ki taare raat ke aasmaan mein chalte hue kyon lagte hain, aur ek taara, Dhruva tara, ek jagah tika hua kyon lagta hai.
answer: Key ideas: the Earth spins from west to east, so stars appear to move from east to west; the Pole Star is almost in line with the Earth's axis, so it seems fixed; the stars themselves are not moving across our sky like that.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: which group of stars helps us find the Pole Star?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kaunsa taaramandal Dhruva tara dhundhne mein madad karta hai?
answer: Saptarishi (Ursa Major or Big Dipper), using its two pointer stars.

subject: science
prompt_en: Which is the largest planet, and which is the smallest?
prompt_hi: Sabse bada grah kaunsa hai aur sabse chhota kaunsa?
answer: Largest: Jupiter. Smallest: Mercury.

subject: science
prompt_en: Make up your own sentence where each word starts with the first letter of a planet, in order: M, V, E, M, J, S, U, N.
prompt_hi: Apna ek vaakya banao jiska har shabd grahon ke pehle akshar se, kram se, shuru ho: M, V, E, M, J, S, U, N.
answer: Any sentence whose word initials are M V E M J S U N in order, e.g. 'My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles'.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: on a clear evening you see Venus and a bright star near it. Which one twinkles more?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: saaf shaam mein tumhe Shukra (Venus) aur uske paas ek chamakdaar taara dikhta hai. Kaun zyada timtimaayega?
answer: The star twinkles; Venus shines steadily, as planets usually do.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: Mercury is nearest the Sun and Venus is second. Which planet is the hottest?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: Budh (Mercury) Suraj ke sabse paas hai aur Shukra (Venus) doosre number pe. Sabse garam grah kaunsa hai?
answer: Venus; its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, making it hotter than Mercury.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: in early January the Earth is at its closest to the Sun all year. Is it summer or winter in India then?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: January ki shuruaat mein Dharti poore saal mein Suraj ke sabse paas hoti hai. Tab Bharat mein garmi hoti hai ya sardi?
answer: Winter; so distance doesn't cause the seasons; the tilt of the Earth's axis does.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said the Moon reflects sunlight. Why then do we see the Moon change shape (phases) during a month?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha chaand Suraj ki roshni reflect karta hai. Toh mahine bhar mein chaand ka aakaar (kalaayein) kyon badalta dikhta hai?
answer: The Moon goes around the Earth, so from Earth we see different amounts of its sunlit half, which makes its shape seem to change.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare Earth and Jupiter: which is bigger, which is closer to the Sun, and what is each mostly made of?
prompt_hi: Dharti aur Brihaspati compare karo: kaun bada hai, kaun Suraj ke paas hai, aur dono zyada-tar kis cheez se bane hain?
answer: Jupiter is much bigger (about 11 Earths across); Earth is closer to the Sun; Earth is rocky while Jupiter is mostly gas.

subject: science
prompt_en: Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander and Pragyan rover ran on solar panels. Why did they have to stop working when night came on the Moon?
prompt_hi: Chandrayaan-3 ke Vikram lander aur Pragyan rover solar panel se chalte the. Chaand pe raat aane pe unhe kaam kyon rokna pada?
answer: They needed sunlight for power; the Moon makes no light of its own, so during the long lunar night (about 14 Earth days) there was no sunlight, and it also becomes extremely cold.

subject: science
prompt_en: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. If the Sun suddenly went dark, how long would it be before we noticed?
prompt_hi: Suraj ki roshni ko Dharti tak pahunchne mein lagbhag 8 minute lagte hain. Agar Suraj achaanak bujh jaaye, toh humein kitni der baad pata chalega?
answer: About 8 minutes, because the light already on its way would keep arriving until then.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw the Sun and the eight planets in order along a line. Make Jupiter the biggest circle and Mercury the smallest. Which planet comes right after Earth?
prompt_hi: Suraj aur aathon grahon ko kram se ek line pe banao. Brihaspati sabse bada gola aur Budh sabse chhota. Dharti ke theek baad kaunsa grah aata hai?
answer: Mars.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'It's hot in May because the Earth goes nearest to the Sun in May.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Mai mein garmi isliye hoti hai kyonki Mai mein Dharti Suraj ke sabse paas jaati hai.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Seasons are caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis: in May the Sun's rays fall more directly on India and the days are longer. The Earth is actually closest to the Sun in January.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your friend the difference between a star and a planet, using the Sun, the Moon and Venus.
prompt_hi: Apne dost ko Suraj, Chaand aur Shukra ke example se taare aur grah ka farak samjhao.
answer: Key ideas: a star like the Sun makes its own light and is a huge ball of hot glowing gas; planets like Venus and moons like our Moon don't make light but reflect sunlight; planets go around the Sun and the Moon goes around the Earth; stars twinkle, planets usually don't.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: which planet comes between Mars and Saturn?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Mangal aur Shani ke beech kaunsa grah aata hai?
answer: Jupiter.

subject: science
prompt_en: Arrange from smallest to largest: the Milky Way, Earth, the universe, the solar system, the Sun.
prompt_hi: Sabse chhote se sabse bade tak lagao: Akashganga, Dharti, brahmaand, saurmandal, Suraj.
answer: Earth, the Sun, the solar system, the Milky Way, the universe.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: you look at the night sky from a big city, then from Hanle in Ladakh, far from city lights. Where can you see the Milky Way, and why?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: tum raat ka aasmaan ek bade shehar se dekhte ho, phir shehar ki roshni se door Ladakh ke Hanle se. Akashganga kahan dikhegi, aur kyon?
answer: From Hanle; its skies are dark, while city lights make the sky bright and hide faint starlight.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: if the Sun were moved as far away as the other stars in the night sky, how would it look?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar Suraj ko utna door le jaaya jaaye jitne raat ke baaki taare hain, toh woh kaisa dikhega?
answer: Like a tiny dot of light, just like the other stars, and not especially bright.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: light from a star takes 100 years to reach us. If that star stopped shining today, when would we notice?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek taare ki roshni ko hum tak pahunchne mein 100 saal lagte hain. Agar woh taara aaj chamakna band kar de, toh humein kab pata chalega?
answer: After about 100 years; we see the star as it was 100 years ago, because its light is still travelling to us.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said the Sun would look like a dot from far away. So why does it look so big to us?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha door se Suraj ek bindu jaisa dikhega. Toh humein woh itna bada kyon dikhta hai?
answer: It is far, far nearer than any other star: about 150 million km away, while the next nearest star is about 4 light-years away.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare the solar system and the Milky Way: what is in each, and how are they connected?
prompt_hi: Saurmandal aur Akashganga compare karo: dono mein kya hai, aur dono ka aapas mein kya rishta hai?
answer: The solar system is the Sun with its planets, moons, asteroids and comets. The Milky Way is billions of stars (many with their own planets) plus gas and dust. The solar system is one tiny part of the Milky Way.

subject: science
prompt_en: Write your full address in space, like a postal address, from your city up to the universe.
prompt_hi: Apna antariksh wala poora pata likho, jaise postal address hota hai, apne shehar se brahmaand tak.
answer: City → state → India → Earth → solar system → Milky Way galaxy → universe.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why do you think India set up a telescope and a 'dark sky reserve' at Hanle in Ladakh, instead of in a big city?
prompt_hi: Tumhe kya lagta hai, Bharat ne telescope aur 'dark sky reserve' bade shehar ki jagah Ladakh ke Hanle mein kyon banaya?
answer: Hanle is high up and dry, with many clear nights and very little light pollution, so faint stars and galaxies can be seen clearly; the reserve protects that darkness.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw circles inside circles: Earth inside the solar system, inside the Milky Way, inside the universe. Label each one.
prompt_hi: Gole ke andar gole banao: Dharti saurmandal ke andar, woh Akashganga ke andar, aur woh brahmaand ke andar. Har ek pe naam likho.
answer: Innermost: Earth; then the solar system; then the Milky Way; outermost: the universe.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'The Sun is the biggest star in the universe; that's why it's the brightest.' Correct him.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Suraj brahmaand ka sabse bada taara hai; isliye sabse chamakdaar hai.' Use sahi karo.
answer: The Sun is a medium-sized star; it looks the brightest only because it is the nearest. Stars like Betelgeuse are hundreds of times wider.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your cousin what the Milky Way is and where we are in it.
prompt_hi: Apne cousin ko samjhao ki Akashganga kya hai aur hum usme kahan hain.
answer: Key ideas: the Milky Way is our galaxy of billions of stars, seen as a faint band in dark skies; our Sun is one star in it, far from its centre; the universe has billions of such galaxies.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: is a light-year a measure of time or of distance?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: light-year samay ka naap hai ya doori ka?
answer: Distance: how far light travels in one year.

subject: sst
prompt_en: What do we call the 0° line of latitude, and the 0° line of longitude?
prompt_hi: 0° latitude wali line ko kya kehte hain, aur 0° longitude wali line ko?
answer: 0° latitude is the Equator; 0° longitude is the Prime Meridian (through Greenwich).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare latitudes and longitudes: which kind of line gets shorter as you move towards the poles, and which kind are all the same length?
prompt_hi: Latitude aur longitude ko compare karo: kaunsi lines poles ki taraf chhoti hoti jaati hain, aur kaunsi sab barabar lambai ki hain?
answer: Latitudes (parallels) get shorter towards the poles (the Equator is the longest); longitudes (meridians) are all the same length, running pole to pole.

subject: sst
prompt_en: A dot is placed at 0° latitude and 0° longitude. Describe in words where it is on the Earth.
prompt_hi: Ek dot 0° latitude aur 0° longitude pe lagaya hai. Shabdon mein batao woh Earth pe kahaan hai?
answer: Where the Equator crosses the Prime Meridian — in the Atlantic Ocean (Gulf of Guinea), off the coast of West Africa.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Mumbai is at about 19°N, 73°E and Kolkata is at about 23°N, 88°E. Which city is farther east, and which is farther north?
prompt_hi: Mumbai lagbhag 19°N, 73°E pe hai aur Kolkata lagbhag 23°N, 88°E pe. Kaunsa sheher zyada east mein hai, aur kaunsa zyada north mein?
answer: Kolkata is farther east (88°E > 73°E) and also farther north (23°N > 19°N).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: Arunachal Pradesh (about 97°E) and western Gujarat (about 68°E) — where does the sun rise first, and roughly how much earlier?
prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo: Arunachal Pradesh (lagbhag 97°E) aur pashchimi Gujarat (lagbhag 68°E) — suraj pehle kahaan ugega, aur lagbhag kitna pehle?
answer: In Arunachal Pradesh, about 2 hours earlier (about 29° difference × 4 minutes per degree ≈ 116 minutes).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why is Indian Standard Time 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich time?
prompt_hi: Indian Standard Time Greenwich time se 5 ghante 30 minute aage kyon hai?
answer: IST is set by the 82.5°E meridian; since 15° = 1 hour, 82.5 ÷ 15 = 5.5 hours, and places to the east are ahead because they meet the sun earlier.
